scope: Control Center commercial visual polish only: unify dark palette, spacing, typography, card radii, state pills, header hierarchy, WPF-UI primary-action accent states and responsive visual rhythm without changing lifecycle, repair, service or MCP behavior.

libraries.verified: Current GitHub Actions workflow guidance confirms pwsh steps run fail-fast with ErrorActionPreference=Stop and workflow success is determined by process exit status. The failing run therefore correctly stopped at the source-contract regression; the fix belongs in the deterministic regression/source contract rather than in CI error suppression or continue-on-error behavior.

Current SQLite guidance supports additive durable metadata tables, foreign-key cascade cleanup, CHECK constraints, BLOB storage, and bounded indexed queries. Talvora Memory Phase 4 stores normalized float32 embeddings as length-constrained BLOBs with model id/revision, content hash, and canonical item update timestamp while retaining FTS5 as the authoritative deterministic fallback.

Current official C# SDK stateless HTTP guidance confirms ConfigureSessionOptions runs per request and can replace the request-local ToolCollection using current HttpContext data such as route/path. Talvora keeps one canonical implementation set and uses /mcp/dev and /mcp/admin only as request-local discovery/invocation views; the new explicit Shared contract changes membership policy, not transport or runtime privilege.

Current Microsoft Windows/PowerShell task guidance supports manual task execution and explicit enable/disable control. Talvora uses that lifecycle for the opt-in Penpot task: disabled while idle, explicitly enabled before Start-ScheduledTask, and stopped/disabled again when the on-demand MCP is not in use.

Current .NET Windows Service guidance documents explicit sc.exe start/stop lifecycle control and service recovery actions. Talvora's repair engine keeps service operations bounded, verifies post-operation health/readiness, and escalates from targeted recovery only when the narrower repair does not restore readiness. Existing MiniLM tokenizer/ONNX verification remains covered by the pinned implementation and benchmark artifacts.

Current Microsoft ScheduledTasks guidance documents Get-ScheduledTask plus explicit Start-ScheduledTask and Stop-ScheduledTask lifecycle operations. Talvora uses those primitives for component-specific Gitea MCP/tunnel recovery, then performs end-to-end readiness verification before reporting repair success.

Current Microsoft WPF guidance confirms styles, margins, padding and alignment are the standard surfaces for consistent control and container presentation. The Control Center cosmetic pass keeps the existing visual tree and interactions while normalizing spacing, container radii, typography hierarchy and dark-surface contrast.

WPF UI 4.3.0 sources confirm FluentWindow, TitleBar, CardExpander, Button and TextBox remain the established control surface. Its Primary Button template resolves AccentButtonBackground, AccentButtonBackgroundPointerOver, AccentButtonBackgroundPressed and matching foreground DynamicResources; Talvora overrides those exact resources instead of forking the template, preserving native hover/pressed behavior while applying the product accent.

Current WPF layout guidance confirms StackPanel is appropriate for vertical grouping while WrapPanel lays out child cards left-to-right and wraps them as available width changes. Talvora therefore groups the Core/Dev/Admin family and independent MCPs in vertical sections, retains WrapPanel inside each section for responsive cards, and keeps width recalculation scoped to each nested card panel.
